question: does the procedure learned from one demonstration transfer ACROSS widget families, or only WITHIN one?
previous_round_answer: within-family transfer proven (click-menu 8/8, click-menu-2 9/10). cross-family untested.

family_B_slider.procedure: drag the slider handle to the pixel corresponding to the target value

family_C_drag.procedure: translate the small box so its top-left lands inside the large box

the_decisive_observation.what_this_shows: the procedure executed. it did not fail to transfer. it produced a WRONG NUMBER every time because the value-to-pixel mapping is not the linear mapping the procedure assumed. target 50 produced 101.
the_decisive_observation.literature_match: ComponentBench (COLM 2026) reports continuous calibration error as the single largest error class at 20.2%, and states these tasks are 'trivial for humans (one drag) yet resistant to added reasoning'. This is that failure mode, reproduced.
the_decisive_observation.why_drag_succeeded: containment is a GEOMETRIC RELATION between two boxes: put this corner inside that rectangle. A relation is expressible as a rule and is valid for every box. Value-to-pixel calibration is a PROPERTY OF THIS WIDGET INSTANCE, which no rule derived from one demonstration can know.

the_first_principles_law_that_this_estab: a procedure transfers across families exactly when the world provides the error signal that lets the procedure self-correct. drag-box gives one: you can measure whether the small box is inside the large one, before submitting. the slider gives none: after dragging you can READ the number off the page, which means the correct procedure is not 'compute the pixel' but 'drag, read the value, correct, repeat'.
the_implication_for_the_users_thesis: instant learning transfers across families WHEN the task admits a closed correction loop (observe the result of your own action and compare it to the goal). It does NOT transfer when the agent must open-loop guess a continuous parameter. The fix is not more learning, and not more verbs: it is making the action OBSERVABLE and CORRECTABLE, which is the same thing that makes the SE case work (compile, run, read the failure).
the_untested_prediction_this_generates: if the slider episode is rewritten as drag -> read #val -> drag again by the residual, it should converge in 1-2 corrections and the family-C result should repeat. That is a falsifiable prediction, not a claim.
what_is_NOT_claimed: that drag works on every drag task
